overview: Two-storey white modern-farmhouse front, about 25 m wide wall-to-wall, facing the street across a raised front yard. GROUND FLOOR, left to right: (1) the garage block - a plain lap-sided wall 6.5 m wide with two white 8 ft carriage-style doors, a black slatted steel canopy on four tie rods above them, a lantern each side, and a stained wood side gate at the far left; it is the most recessed ground-floor wall. (2) A deep covered porch on a ledgestone-clad base, 4 risers above the yard, with a bluestone floor, square white 0.3 m columns and a white box beam. Its left bay stands in front of the office (two-panel glazed door), whose wall is ~1.2 m forward of the garage; the middle is a recessed entry alcove (navy 9 ft Dutch-style door with two sidelights) under a slightly projecting pyramid-hipped roof, reached by a 2.6 m wide flight of 4 bluestone steps between stone piers; the right bay fronts the living room (four-part French door unit) and is ~1 m shallower. A second small flight of steps leaves the porch's west end to the driveway. (3) A one-storey wing at the right end which steps forward of the living-room wall: its west side wall (single glass door onto the porch) closes the porch, and its front has a board-and-batten box bay with a wide triple window, a second black canopy, two lanterns and a small decorative gable sitting on the roof above. ROOFS AT FIRST-FLOOR LEVEL: one continuous black standing-seam skirt with a single eave height wraps the garage, porch, entry, right bay, wing and both side walls; the sloping planes are only ~2 m deep and hide a flat membrane roof behind them. UPPER FLOOR (narrower than the ground floor, set well back on the left and middle): on the left a board-and-batten gable bay with a twin window rises out of the garage roof; then two recessed lap-sided walls (wall A with a short wide window and a tall narrow one, wall B 0.65 m further back with a tall twin unit) under the eave of the main shingled hip roof; on the right a gabled block comes forward ~2.7 m, with its own projecting board-and-batten gable bay and twin window, a small window on its west side wall, and a tall white lap-sided chimney with a black metal bonnet cap at its front-right corner; right of the chimney a short recessed wall with a small square window ends the upper storey. Upper roofs are charcoal dimensional shingles; gutters and downspouts are black. GROUNDS: paver driveway on the left rising ~1 m from the street to the garage; curved bluestone walk from the entry steps to the driveway; lawn panels; a ~1.1 m ledgestone retaining wall with a light cap along the street (street skewed ~7 deg to the house), a row of globe shrubs on top and three young standard trees in the strip at its foot.

relations: Left to right at ground level (street view): side gate | garage block with 2 doors | (office block steps forward ~1.2 m) porch-left bay with the office door | recessed entry alcove with the front door | right porch bay with the living-room French doors | one-storey wing with a box bay and triple window | east side gate.

Depth datum = garage front wall plane (0 m, + toward the street). Estimated plane depths (+-0.5 m; from top-down p30 eave positions corrected for roof height, cross-checked with p01 lap-siding course sizes and drone frames): office front wall +1.2; entry/living wall -0.3; porch-left column line (outer face) +3.45; entry column line +3.7; right-bay column line +2.6; wing main front wall +1.65; wing box-bay face +2.25; upper wall A -2.1; upper wall B -2.75; upper-left gable bay face -1.6; right upper block front wall ~0.0; right upper gable bay face +0.7; recessed upper-right wall -0.75.

The garage front wall is therefore the most recessed ground-floor wall on the left; the porch roof projects ~3.3 m beyond the garage eave (p30: garage eave y=1998, porch-left eave y=2183, entry eave y=2195, right-bay eave y=2134, wing bay eave y=2117, wing main / east eave corner y=2085).
The entry roof eave is only ~0.24 m in front of the porch-left eave but ~1.1 m in front of the right-bay eave; column_3_rear stands ~1.1 m directly behind column_3_front on the right-bay beam line.

The entry door wall is recessed ~1.5 m behind the office front wall (p01 course size 10.6 px vs 11.65 px on adjacent walls); the living-room French doors are in the same plane as the entry door (continuous wall in p02).
Porch clear depths wall-to-column-outer-face: ~2.25 m in front of the office, ~4.0 m at the entry, ~2.9 m in front of the living room.

All low roofs (garage, porch, entry, right bay, wing and the west/east side skirts) are one continuous black standing-seam system with the eave at one height: gutter top ~4.0 m above the garage slab = ~3.6 m above the porch floor. The garage slab is therefore ~0.4 m below the porch/main floor.
The porch floor is 4 risers (~0.66 m) above the front walk and lawn; porch columns are ~3.06 m from floor to beam soffit.
Behind the standing-seam skirts there is a flat membrane roof between the porch roofs and upper walls A / B; the standing-seam planes are only ~2 m deep in plan and stop at that flat roof.

The upper storey is narrower than the ground floor: in p01 it spans x 382 (left corner) to x 2088 (right corner) while the ground floor spans x 152 to x 2431. On the left the garage extends ~2.5 m beyond the upper storey; on the right the one-storey wing extends ~3.7 m beyond it.

Upper-left gable bay is centred over the garage width only roughly: bay x 431-709 vs garage wall x 152-787 in p01 (bay centre ~100 px right of the garage centre); its window sill sits right on the garage roof flashing.

Right upper gable bay (x 1579-1823 in p01) stands above the junction of the entry and the right porch bay; its centre is ~70 px right of the entry roof's right corner region and its base sits on the flat roof / top of the right-bay roof.
Upper wall B is ~0.65 m behind upper wall A (p30 eave step 37 px); the right upper block's front wall is ~2.7 m in front of wall B (its west side wall is ~2.4 m long).

The chimney is at the front-right corner of the right upper block: front face about flush with that block's front wall (within ~0.2 m), right edge ~0.5 m beyond the block's east wall, shaft top ~0.65 m and cap top ~1.4 m above the right gable ridge.

The recessed upper-right wall (with the small square window) is ~0.8 m behind the right block's front wall and butts against the right side of the chimney; the wing roof ridge/hip rises to just below its window.

The wing box bay projects ~0.6 m from the wing main wall; porch column 4 stands ~0.9 m in front of the wing main wall, roughly in line with (0.3 m ahead of) the bay face. The wing's west wall with the single door is ~1.95 m long.

Window head heights: upper-left bay window and right bay window heads are at the same image height (y 837 in p01); the entry door head is ~0.34 m higher than the French-door and office-door heads (9 ft vs 8 ft).
Garage canopy top is ~0.4 m above the garage door head and ~0.6 m below the soffit; the wing canopy underside is ~0.15 m above the triple-window head.

All eleven visible front sconces are the same fixture: left and right of the garage doors, on porch columns 1, 2, 3(front) and 4, on the wall right of the entry door, and either side of the wing window.

Street wall is not parallel to the house: in p30 its outer face runs from (600,2471) to (1500,2358), i.e. the street is rotated ~7 deg; front yard depth from the entry eave to the wall is ~4.7 m at the entry and ~4.4 m at the wing; the garage door is ~9 m from the street edge.

p01 is not exactly square-on: the facade recedes to the right (eave lines converge to the right, horizontal scale falls from ~1.04x to ~0.92x of the vertical scale left to right); the camera is roughly opposite the garage/office junction, ~25-30 m away, low (about 0.4 m above the garage slab level).
